title: Why Sanitary Tees Fail in Horizontal Drainage
description: Using a standard sanitary tee to connect horizontal drain lines is a widespread installation error in drainage systems. Sanitary tees are designed primarily for transitioning from a horizontal branch into a vertical stack. When installed horizontally, the short directional sweep fails to channel waste smoothly, leading to solids accumulating, frequent blockages, and potential backflow. For horizontal-to-horizontal branch connections, proper drainage principles require a wye fitting or a combination wye and eighth bend. This creates a gradual sweep that maintains flow velocity and prevents waste buildup, ensuring code compliance and reliable long-term performance.
